chunks: Bakr ibn Muḥammad al-Azdī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
"I dislike it for a man to pray behind the Imam in a prayer in which the recitation is not uttered aloud, and then stand as though he were a donkey."
He said: I said, "May I be your ransom, then what should he do?" He said: "He should engage in tasbīḥ."

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.يُسَبِّحُ: he engages in tasbih, glorifying Allah

ai.seo_question: What should a person do while praying behind the Imam in a silent congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs that a follower in congregational salat, during prayers in which the Imam does not recite aloud, should not remain idle. Instead, he should occupy himself with tasbih. The report reflects etiquette and legal guidance for participation in silent congregational prayer.
